response: Yes, socioeconomic status (SES) can significantly impact the quality of life in lung cancer patients. Studies have shown that patients with lower SES tend to have poorer health outcomes, reduced access to healthcare services, and lower quality of life compared to those with higher SES. Factors such as limited financial resources, lower education levels, and lack of health insurance can exacerbate the challenges faced by lung cancer patients, affecting their ability to receive timely and effective treatment, manage symptoms, and cope with the emotional and psychological aspects of the disease. Additionally, socioeconomic disparities can also influence patients' access to supportive care services, such as palliative care, rehabilitation, and mental health support, which are essential for maintaining quality of life during and after treatment.
